# Data Protection and Privacy (DATA)

Rules for personal and business data, including the obligations of Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020 (PDPL). Its Executive Regulations were issued by Ministerial Decree No. 816 of 2025 (in force 2 November 2025), with about one year for organizations to comply.

## SCS-DATA-01 Classify data and handle it according to its classification

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Every application MUST identify the personal and sensitive business data it processes, classify it under the ISMS data classification policy, and apply the controls that classification requires (encryption, masking, access, retention). Sensitive data at rest MUST be encrypted.

Implementation (all stacks):

- List each data field with its classification (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and whether it is personal data or sensitive personal data under PDPL, in the application's data inventory.
- Apply Microsoft Purview / Azure Information Protection (AIP) labels and DLP rules to documents and exports where the organization uses them.
- Mask sensitive values in screens and reports where the full value is not needed (for example last 4 digits only).

Implementation (Flutter):

- Do not store sensitive business data in plain text on the device (see SCS-MOB-02).

Verification: Data inventory exists for the application and matches the database schema; spot-check that sensitive fields are encrypted and masked.

## SCS-DATA-02 Collect and keep only the personal data you need

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Applications MUST collect only the personal data strictly needed for a declared purpose, keep it no longer than that purpose and the Data Retention Policy require, and then delete or anonymize it. Where PDPL requires consent, the application MUST record the user's consent and support the data subject rights (access, correction, erasure, objection, withdrawal of consent).

Implementation (all stacks):

- Document the purpose and legal basis (consent, contract, legal obligation) for each personal data field in the data inventory.
- Implement retention: scheduled jobs that delete or anonymize expired records, following the Data Retention Policy (for example tax records for 7 years).
- Provide a way (admin function or documented procedure) to export, correct and erase a person's data when the Data Protection Officer requests it.
- Sensitive personal data (health, biometric, children's data, and others listed in PDPL) needs explicit written consent and a license from the Personal Data Protection Center; involve the DPO before collecting it.
- Do not transfer personal data outside Egypt (including to cloud or AI services hosted abroad) without DPO approval, as PDPL requires a license or permit for cross-border transfer.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Request only the device permissions the feature needs (MASVS-PRIVACY-1); explain why in the permission prompt.
- Do not send device identifiers, contacts or location to analytics unless the purpose is documented and approved.

Verification: DPO / ISMS review of the data inventory for new applications; retention job exists and runs.

## SCS-DATA-03 Support personal data breach notification

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Applications that process personal data MUST log enough to determine what data, whose data and when, if a breach happens. Any suspected personal data breach MUST be reported immediately to IT Security and the Data Protection Officer, so the Personal Data Protection Center can be notified within 72 hours and affected people within 3 working days of that notice, as PDPL requires.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Log access to and exports of personal data with user, time and record scope (see SCS-LOG-01), without logging the personal data itself.
- Include the DPO in the incident runbook for each application that processes personal data.

Verification: Incident runbook names the DPO and the 72-hour deadline. Access logs show who exported personal data.
